pensamiento:
I'm checking QUS-001 and QUS-003, which both pass. QUS-002 covers two things, disabling biometrics and the password, but they serve one objective, a PIN login, so I'd still call it compliant. QUS-004's benefit, "entrar más rápido a la app," is the part I still need to judge.

I'm going through the rest of the list: QUS-005 prescribes the PIN as the solution rather than stating the need, so I'm leaning toward a minor defect there. QUS-006's "más rápido" has no measure, which makes it a major defect. Now I'm checking QUS-007 against the BAN rules.

I'm marking QUS-008 and QUS-009 as compliant, since there's no duplicate and the format is uniform. For the INV items, INV-001 and INV-002 look fine, but INV-003 is missing PIN rules like lockout and recovery, and INV-005 has no acceptance criteria, which makes it a blocking gap. I'll come back to DOR-001's dependency on the existing login once I've checked it.

I'm still weighing whether DOR-001's dependency on the existing biometric and password functions counts as a defect, and I'm leaning against flagging it since nothing external is involved. For DOR-002, the 4-digit PIN length is stated, but the attempt limit, lockout, recovery, and storage rules are not.

I'm marking DOR-003 as a minor defect, since login is critical functionality and no measurable non-functional requirement is given. BM-001 is a blocking defect, because removing biometrics and the password leaves only a 4-digit PIN as the authentication. BM-002 is a major defect, since the session behavior for the changed login is never defined.

I'm weighing whether the PIN storage gap for BM-004 counts as a defect, since the story is silent on where the PIN lives rather than contradicting any control, so I'm leaning toward flagging it as a question for the analyst instead of a defect.

I'm weighing whether changing the login method counts as a change to the client's security data, and I'm inclined to flag it as a major defect, though I want to avoid over-flagging. I'm also checking BM-006: the HU changes the login screen into a PIN screen, so the accessibility requirement applies, and it's not mentioned, which makes it a minor defect.

I'm checking BM-007 next: the login relies on the network, and the error case isn't defined, so that's a major gap. BM-008 uses the device biometric function that's being removed, and the story doesn't address both platforms, so I'm marking that as a minor gap. BM-009 doesn't apply, since the PIN is a credential rather than newly collected personal data.

I'm leaning toward treating DOR-001 as not applicable, since the dependency is on existing biometric and password functions rather than an external system. I'm also judging the login-screen question and the logic around the INV-004 estimate. I want to estimate the scope, which covers switching login methods, creating the PIN, and disabling biometrics and the password along with the security rules, before deciding how to report it.

I'm weighing whether to estimate this story at 5 or 3, since the scope of the login flow changes around PIN and security rules is still unclear. I'm leaning toward 5 as a provisional estimate because it touches biometrics, password and PIN storage, but the story doesn't define a clear scope, which the instructions say should be recorded as 1.

I'm going with a 5 on this story, since the change to login methods can be sized even though the PIN rules are still missing. I've listed 13 defects, several of them blocking, so I'm going to send it back with a recommendation for each one.

I'm settling on the story's refined wording now, since I'm sending it back and the acceptance criteria can stay empty for a return. I'm trying to keep the "Como / quiero / para" format without adding any scope the story doesn't already state, and I'm weighing whether to keep the PIN in the wording or leave it out so the story doesn't assume a solution.

I'm keeping the refined story wording with the PIN, since the biometric question is a scope decision for the analyst and the recommendation will flag it as pending. Thirteen defects are logged, and none of them duplicate each other: BAN-01 and BAN-03 conflict, so I'll note that under QUS-007. Next I'm registering the revision as functional.

recomendaciones.texto: La HU elimina la biometría y la contraseña y deja solo un PIN de 4 dígitos, lo que debilita la autenticación existente. Definir el factor de autenticación de la operación de ingreso (y de la reautenticación para operaciones sensibles) o mantener biometría o contraseña como factor.
Conflicta con BAN-01 y BAN-03, que exigen ingreso con huella o reconocimiento facial. Antes de continuar, el producto debe decidir cuál prevalece; la HU no debe elegir por sí sola.
El enunciado impone la solución (PIN de 4 dígitos). Describir la necesidad (ingreso más ágil con un método de seguridad definido) y dejar el método como decisión a validar.
'Más rápido' es vago. Expresar el beneficio con una medida, por ejemplo un tiempo máximo de ingreso medido en un escenario definido.
Faltan reglas para estimar: longitud y formato del PIN, política de cambio, qué pasa con los usuarios que ya tienen biometría o contraseña, y si se pueden reactivar.
No hay criterios de aceptación. Agregar criterios observables, por ejemplo: 'Con PIN correcto, el cliente ingresa a la app' y 'Con PIN incorrecto, no ingresa y se muestra un mensaje'.
No se definen intentos fallidos permitidos, bloqueo, tiempo de espera ni recuperación de PIN olvidado. Definir cada regla con valores concretos o marcadores como [INTENTOS].
Al ser el ingreso una funcionalidad crítica, declarar al menos un requisito no funcional medible (por ejemplo, tiempo de respuesta del ingreso o protección contra fuerza bruta).
Como cambia el ingreso, definir el comportamiento de la sesión: expiración por inactividad, reautenticación al volver de segundo plano y cierre de sesión.
El cambio del método de autenticación modifica datos de seguridad del cliente. Indicar qué eventos se registran para auditoría (quién, qué, cuándo, dispositivo) sin datos sensibles en claro.
La HU cambia la pantalla de ingreso. Mencionar que la nueva pantalla cumple accesibilidad (lector de pantalla, contraste, tamaño de texto) con WCAG 2.1 AA.
Definir qué pasa sin conexión, con red lenta o con error del servicio durante el ingreso, y que no se pueda reintentar de forma que duplique operaciones.
La HU desactiva funciones del dispositivo (biometría). Indicar el comportamiento en iOS y en Android, y las versiones mínimas.
